help:
/whatnow                 show or hide
/whatnow side            put it at the side (or above the prompt if the window is narrow)
/whatnow band            put it above the prompt again
/whatnow limit 120k      tokens at which the handoff is requested (now: {L}k)
/whatnow progress        Claude updates PROGRESS.md now
/whatnow handoff         Claude writes the handoff now
/whatnow en | es | auto  language (auto detects it)
/whatnow help            this list
instructions:
This project keeps a file {progress} at its root that feeds the whatnow panel. Create it if missing and keep it up to date whenever the current task changes or something is completed. Write all the text in this file (goal, Status, tasks) in English. Exact format:

# <project goal in one line>
Status: <one sentence on how we are doing overall>

- [x] task done
- [ ] task pending

## This session [{mark}]
Task: <one sentence on this conversation's task>
- [x] step of this conversation's task, done
- [ ] step pending

Project % comes from the checkboxes above (they cover the whole project) and Session % from those under "## This session" (only this conversation's task). Your section is the one whose heading carries the mark [{mark}]; other sessions of this project have theirs with another mark: do not touch them. When a new conversation starts, empty and rewrite your section with its task; create it if missing. Do not write in the "## Haiku [mark]" sections: they belong to a small model that notes there what it thinks. This file is single for the whole project: if you work in a parallel copy (folder .claude/worktrees/<name>), still write in this same file (the one in the main folder), in your section.
handoffPrompt: {why} Before continuing, write the handoff in {handoff} so another session with no memory can continue: goal, what we were doing and why, decisions made (and which ones the person made), files touched with their path, what is left and the concrete next step. Also update {progress}, and keep your section "## This session [{mark}]" (leave it with the next task and no steps done); do not touch the sections of other sessions that are still open. The "## This session [mark]" sections of {progress} whose mark is not in this list of sessions open right now belong to sessions that are already closed: [{live}] (if the list is empty, touch none). Before deleting them, read them and move into the project list what they left done or pending and still matters; then delete them. Haiku, a small model, writes after every turn only in its own section "## Haiku [mark]" of {progress}, and only about the session (its task, the steps it thinks are done and new steps); it can be wrong. The project is yours to update: with what you really know about the session and what Haiku left pending, bring the project list and your section up to date (tick what is really done, add what is worth it, decide what belongs to the project and what only to the session) and discard what is false or you cannot tell. Then delete every "## Haiku [mark]" section there is, yours included. Also merge repeated tasks and remove what no longer applies. Then tell the person they can /clear (or open another session) and the new one will read the handoff by itself.
progressNow: Update {progress} right now with the real state of the project (create it if missing, in the format you know): goal, Status and the complete list of done and pending tasks, plus your section "## This session [{mark}]" (leave other sessions' sections alone) with its one-sentence "Task:" line and its list. Haiku, a small model, writes after every turn only in its own section "## Haiku [mark]" of {progress}, and only about the session (its task, the steps it thinks are done and new steps); it can be wrong. The project is yours to update: with what you really know about the session and what Haiku left pending, bring the project list and your section up to date (tick what is really done, add what is worth it, decide what belongs to the project and what only to the session) and discard what is false or you cannot tell. Then delete every "## Haiku [mark]" section there is, yours included. Also merge repeated tasks and remove what no longer applies. Then summarize in one line what you changed. Write its text in English, translating what is already there.
